_readme: rules: shown on The Rules page, in order. classifier: the Classify a Food questions. Each option either points to the next question (next) or ends on a taxonomy node id (result). Adding a question here changes the classifier; no code changes needed.

rules.title: The placement key
rules.summary: Five kingdoms, checked in order. The first one that matches wins.
points: Condimenta: made to be applied to other food, never the star. "Made" means extracted, refined, fermented or combined, so the original would not recognize it. Grown things are never condiments.
Liquida: has a beverage role (hydrate, refresh, stimulate, intoxicate).
Naturalia: one whole food, or one nature made (salt, honey), bossed around but still recognizable.
Constructa: assembled food, where the originals can't recognize themselves or several foods share the job.
Incertae sedis: nobody can place it. Pending review, indefinitely.
rules.example: Orange juice is a single ingredient, but it is drunk, so Liquida wins before Naturalia is checked. A lemon is never made, so Condimenta passes it by and it lands in Naturalia, however it is used.

rules.title: The police lineup test
rules.summary: Could the original food pick the result out of a police lineup? If yes, it is Naturalia. If no, it is Constructa.
points: A cucumber can identify a pickle, so pickles are Naturalia.
Flour cannot identify toast, so toast is Constructa.
Smashing the whole food passes: peanut butter is still peanuts. Extracting a part fails: juice, oil and refined sugar are made.
Nature-made counts as one food: salt, honey.
In Naturalia the family and genus are the real ones of the living source: Bos, Vitis, Citrus, Arachis.
rules.example: A raisin is a grape with life experience. The grape would know.

rules.title: The table rule
rules.summary: Nothing the eater does at the table changes a classification. A food is what it was when it arrived.
points: A lemon squeezed over fish and chips is still a lemon.
A New York slice folded by the eater is still a pizza. Folded by the baker, it is a calzone, and a calzone is a sandwich.
Salt sprinkled on a steak is salt visiting a steak.
A cookie dunked in milk is still a cookie. The milk is still milk.
rules.example: The baker's choices count; the eater's do not. That is why the calzone is a sandwich and the folded slice is not.

rules.title: Role beats ingredients
rules.summary: The role a food plays at the table decides drink versus food, not whether you sip it or spoon it.
points: Food role (meal, course, snack, dessert): Constructa, even if drunk through a straw.
Beverage role (hydrate, refresh, stimulate, intoxicate): Liquida, even if assembled.
rules.example: A milkshake is a dessert wearing a straw, so it sits with gazpacho in Immersa. A cocktail is assembled, but it is still a drink. Bubble tea is chewed, so it sits with cereal.

rules.title: The drink test
rules.summary: Drinks are sorted by how they were made, not by why you drink them or what they come in.
points: Ready-made by nature (water, animal milk): Nativa.
Squeezed, pressed or strained from a plant (juice, oat milk): Expressa.
Steeped or pushed through, then strained (coffee, espresso, tea, chai): Infusa.
Things dissolved into water or milk (soda, lemonade, sports drinks, hot chocolate): Soluta.
Microbes did the work (beer, wine): Fermentata.
Two finished drinks mixed in real proportion into a new one with its own name (latte, americano, cocktails): Miscellae.
Restoration rule: water put back where it was taken out restores a drink; it does not make a new one. Orange juice from concentrate is still juice.
Still or sparkling is decided one level down, at order.
rules.example: Lemonade is not juice: it is mostly water with things dissolved in. Oat milk is not milk: it is pressed from a plant. A latte is not coffee: it is two drinks mixed. A milkshake is not a drink at all. Espresso is not Expressa either: the water gets pressed, not the bean. Hot chocolate is not Infusa: the cocoa stays in the cup. Bubble tea is not a drink: you chew it. An americano is a drink of drinks: espresso plus water, a finished drink plus a finished drink.

rules.title: The condiment test
rules.summary: Condiments are sorted by how they were made, like drinks. When methods stack, the last transforming step decides.
points: Purified to crystals (sugar, MSG): Crystallina.
Several foods ground, pounded or chopped together (mustard, relish, salsa): Contrita.
Fermented (soy sauce, vinegar): Zymota.
Emulsified (mayonnaise, Caesar): Emulsa.
Cooked down (ketchup, jelly): Reducta.
Form (dry, pourable, spreadable) is decided one level down, at order.
Finishing steps such as straining and bottling do not count. MSG is fermented, then purified: it sits with the crystals.
rules.example: Hot sauce splits, correctly: an aged, fermented one is Zymota; a cooked and blended one is Reducta. Same shelf, different method. And jelly is jam that lost its identity.

rules.title: The assembly rule
rules.summary: A combination is classified by the structure it forms, not by its parts. If it is built to be eaten as one thing and ordered by one name, it is one specimen. The parts keep their own cards.
points: Side by side (a frank next to a bun on a plate): two specimens. A meal, not a food. Served together on purpose, it is an association (see the next rule).
One on top of another (toppings on one slice): Apertae, open-faced.
One holds the other (a frank in a bun): a new species, in Involucra.
Tossed together (chicken Caesar salad): Mixta.
Cooked together into a liquid: soup, in Decocta.
Something added on (ketchup on the hot dog): a variety, not a new species.
rules.example: "A hot dog is just a sausage and a bun." And a BLT is just bacon and bread: if assembly does not count, no sandwich exists, including the ones everyone agrees on. Biology agrees. A lichen is a fungus and an alga living as one, and it is named after the fungus, its structural partner. Take the frank out and you have two specimens again: a frank and a disappointed bun. Food speciation is reversible, but only before the first bite.

rules.title: The association rule
rules.summary: The menu name never creates a specimen. It only names one the structure test has already found. Foods served together that the eater can still take in separate bites form an association, not a species.
points: The test: can the eater take separate bites? If yes, an association. If not, one specimen, placed by the assembly rule.
Steak frites: the steak and the fries are separate bites. An association.
Poutine: the gravy and curds cannot be eaten apart from the fries. One specimen.

Chicken and waffles: separate bites, whether stacked or side by side. An association, whatever the plating. Resting one food on another does not join them; baking, melting, saucing, wrapping or holding does.
Picking the pepperoni off a pizza is not a separate bite. It is dismantling a specimen, and the table rule ignores it.

Members keep their own cards and their own classification. The association gets a card outside the tree, named as ecologists name plant associations: after its dominant members, ending in -etum (a beech wood is a Fagetum).
Condiments on the plate (béarnaise with steak frites) are applied, not members. Inedible members, such as a kids' meal toy, are commensals: noted, never classified.
rules.example: The Costco hot dog's diagnostic $1.50 buys a hot dog and a soda. The hot dog is still the variety; the $1.50 deal is its type association. If the price changes, both go extinct together.

rules.title: The container test
rules.summary: A sandwich is a filling held between bread: bread on opposite sides of the filling. When one food holds another, the container's material decides the class, and sandwiches are then sorted by their bread all the way down.
points: Slices taken from a loaf: Partiformes, the classic.

One whole roll, bun, tortilla, pizza dough or batter coating per sandwich, however it is cut, hinged, folded or sealed: Integriformes. The hot dog, the burger, the taco, the burrito and the calzone all live here.
Below that, the kind of bread decides the family (buns and rolls, tortillas, fried batter), and only then does the filling's shape decide the genus: tubes, discs, spheres, chunks, sheets.
Classify food as prepared, not as eaten. Folding your own pizza slice is proper technique, not reclassification. Cutting a roll in half before or after building the sandwich changes nothing.

Topped foods are sorted the same way: a slice from a loaf (the open-faced sandwich), or a whole base made for the dish (every pizza). Then the kind of base: hand-shaped crust, pan-shaped crust, formed rice.
Boiled or steamed dough: Dumplingae. Gyoza, ravioli, and the steamed bao.
Pressed rice: Sushiae. The California roll.
Pastry: Pieae. The pot pie.
A whole food (lettuce, banana): Pseudosandwichae. Nice try.
Bread on only one side: not a container at all. It is a topped food in Apertae.
rules.example: What is bread? Ground grain made into dough, then baked, griddled or fried. A hard taco shell is fried, so it counts. Sushi rice keeps its grains whole, so a California roll has sandwich architecture but is sushi.

rules.title: They stand or fall together
rules.summary: Foods with the same structure get the same ruling. You cannot accept one and reject the other.
points: Hot dogs and tacos are both whole bread around a filling. Expel one and the other goes too, along with the burger.
Open-faced sandwiches and pizza share the one-sided shape. Neither is a sandwich.
A pizza folded by the eater is still a pizza. A pizza folded by the baker is a calzone, and a calzone is a sandwich.
rules.example: A court once ruled that one tortilla is not two slices of bread. A hot dog bun is one piece, too.

rules.title: The soup test
rules.summary: Soup is solids in a liquid where either the two were cooked together after assembly, or the liquid is a broth simmered from ingredients. Either may be served cold later.
points: Cooked together after assembly: soup. Chowder, stew, oatmeal.
Served in a broth simmered from ingredients: soup. Restaurant ramen, pho.
Boiling water poured over noodles cooks them in place: cup noodles are soup.
Neither: not soup. Cereal (milk is not a broth), gazpacho (never cooked).
rules.example: Cereal and ramen are both solids in a bowl of liquid. Ramen's liquid is a broth simmered for hours; cereal's is milk from a carton. One is soup, and it is not the cereal.

rules.title: The vessel does not count
rules.summary: Foods are classified by how they are built, not by what they are cooked or served in.
points: A casserole is a pan, not a phylum: layered casseroles go to Stratifica, mixed ones to Mixta.
A cup of noodles is soup because of what happens inside the cup, not because of the cup.
A bread bowl is still a bowl. The chowder inside is under review.
rules.example: Lasagna and tuna noodle casserole are both baked in the same dish. One is layered, one is mixed, so they land in different phyla.

rules.title: Add-ins make varieties, not species
rules.summary: If you would still order it by its base name, an add-in creates a variety, not a new species.
points: A splash into a drink that keeps its name is an add-in: coffee with cream is still coffee. Two drinks combined in real proportion, under a new name, are a drink of drinks: a latte, an americano.
A latte is ordered by a different name: a separate species.
More or less of the same thing is a variety, even with its own name: a doppio, ristretto or lungo is still espresso.
An affogato changes role to dessert: it leaves Liquida entirely.

A topping combination found on many styles is described once, under the style where it was first recorded: its type locality. A Hawaiian on a Detroit crust is the same variety, found in another habitat.
rules.example: A Costco hot dog is still ordered as "a hot dog," so it is a variety of Canis farcitus.

kingdom.question: What job does it do at the table?
kingdom.help: Pick the first one that fits. Order matters.

options.label: It was made to go on other food: a sauce, dressing, jelly or spice blend (not something grown, like salt or a lemon)
You drink it to hydrate, refresh, wake up or unwind
It is one food, or one nature made (salt, honey): maybe dried, ground, pickled or grilled, but still recognizable
Several foods combined, or ingredients turned into something new
It defies explanation
Ingredients fused into one new mass (bread, pasta, sausage, cheese)
One food is the container and holds a filling
Layers or toppings on a base, with no container
Solids sitting in a liquid
Tossed together, no architecture

container.question: What is the container made of?
container.help: Bread is ground grain made into dough, then baked, griddled or fried. Fried counts.

options.label: Bread: a bun, roll, tortilla, taco shell or batter
Boiled or steamed dough: a dumpling wrapper, pasta or steamed bun
Pressed sushi rice
Pastry: pie crust or puff pastry
A whole food: lettuce, a pepper, a banana
One base with toppings on top
Several stacked layers

liquid.question: How did the liquid meet the solids?
liquid.help: Serving it cold later is fine. What matters is whether it was ever cooked, and whether the liquid is a broth.

options.label: They were cooked together after being combined
The liquid is a broth simmered from ingredients, added at the end
Neither: a plain liquid like milk, juice or a raw blend

drink.question: How was the drink made?
drink.help: Ignore the container and why you drink it. Only how it was made matters.

options.label: Nature made it ready to drink: water, animal milk
Squeezed, pressed or strained from a plant: juice, oat milk
Steeped in hot water, then strained: coffee, tea
Sugar, flavor or salts dissolved into water: soda, lemonade, sports drinks
Fermented by yeast or bacteria: beer, wine
Two finished drinks mixed together: latte, cocktail

portion.question: How much bread does one sandwich use?
portion.help: Ignore any cutting. A roll cut in half before or after is still one roll.

options.label: A few slices from a loaf
One whole roll, bun, tortilla or batter coating

base.question: What is the base?
base.help: Ignore any cutting or folding by the eater.

options.label: A slice cut from a larger loaf
A whole base made for this dish: a pizza crust, a pad of rice

condiment.question: How was it made?
condiment.help: Pick the last step that changed it. Straining and bottling do not count.

options.label: Purified to crystals: sugar, MSG
Several foods ground, pounded or chopped together: mustard, relish, salsa
Fermented: soy sauce, vinegar, aged hot sauce
Emulsified: mayonnaise, Caesar, ranch
Cooked down: ketchup, jelly, BBQ sauce
A plant: fruit, seed, nut, leaf or root
An animal, or made by one: meat, fish, honey
The earth: salt
